definition: sextant is a [doubly reflecting navigation instrument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reflecting_instrument) that measures the [angular distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_distance) between two visible objects.

Sierpiński triangle, also called the Sierpiński gasket or Sierpiński sieve, is a [fractal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fractal) with the overall shape of an [equilateral triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equilateral_triangle), subdivided [recursively](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recursion) into smaller equilateral triangles.
similarity system of triangles is a specific configuration involving a set of triangles.

sine wave, sinusoidal wave, or sinusoid (symbol: ∿) is a [periodic wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodic_function) whose [waveform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waveform) (shape) is the [trigonometric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trigonometric_function) [sine function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sine).

Sines Tecnopolo is a [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal) [science park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_park) headquartered in [Sines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sines,_Portugal).

Singmaster's conjecture is a [conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjecture) in [combinatorial number theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combinatorial_number_theory), named after the British mathematician [David Singmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Singmaster) who proposed it in 1971.

Small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) is an [experimental technique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analytical_technique) that uses [elastic neutron scattering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elastic_neutron_scattering) at small scattering angles to investigate the structure of various substances at a [mesoscopic scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesoscopic_scale) of about 1–100 Benoît, Henri: Polymers and neutron scattering. Oxford: Clarendon Press (1994?).

Small-angle scattering (SAS) is a [scattering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scattering) technique based on deflection of [collimated radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collimated_radiation) away from the straight [trajectory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trajectory) after it interacts with structures that are much larger than the [wavelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavelength) of the radiation.
Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) is a [small-angle scattering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small-angle_scattering) technique by which nanoscale density differences in a sample can be quantified.

Snellius–Pothenot problem is a [trigonometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trigonometry) problem first described in the context of planar [surveying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surveying) where known points are used to solve an unknown one.

Solution of triangles () is the main [trigonometric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trigonometry) problem of finding the characteristics of a [triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangle) (angles and lengths of sides), when some of these are known.

special right triangle is a [right triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_triangle) with some notable feature that makes calculations on the [triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangle) easier, or for which simple formulas exist.

spidron is a continuous [flat geometric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plane_geometry) figure composed entirely of [triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangle)s, where, for every pair of joining triangles, each has a leg of the other as one of its legs, and neither has any point inside the interior of the other.

Squigonometry or -trigonometry is a generalization of traditional [trigonometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trigonometry) which replaces the [circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle) and [Euclidean distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_distance) function with the [squircle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squircle) (shape intermediate between a [square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square) and circle) and [[Norm (mathematics)#p-norm|-norm]].
Stephen Thomas Buchanan (March 4, 1903 – November 21, 1992) was an American [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football) player.

suboccipital triangles are a paired triangular-shaped space of the upper posterior [neck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neck) bounded by the following three paired muscles of the [suboccipital set of muscles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suboccipital_muscles): * [Rectus capitis posterior major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rectus_capitis_posterior_major) - above and medially * [Obliquus capitis superior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obliquus_capitis_superior) - above and laterally * [Obliquus capitis inferior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obliquus_capitis_inferior) - below and laterally (Rectus capitis posterior minor is also one of the suboccipital muscles but does not form part of the triangle) It is covered by a layer of dense fibro-fatty tissue, situated beneath the [semispinalis capitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semispinalis_capitis).
supraclavicular fossa is an indentation (fossa) immediately above the [clavicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clavicle).

Sylvester's theorem or Sylvester's formula describes a particular interpretation of the sum of three pairwise distinct [vectors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_(mathematics_and_physics)) of equal length in the context of [triangle geometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangle_geometry).

ternary plot, ternary graph, triangle plot, simplex plot, or Gibbs triangle is a [barycentric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barycentric_coordinates_(mathematics)) [plot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plot_(graphics)) on three variables which [sum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summation) to a constant.

Texas Triangle is one of eleven [megaregions of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megaregions_of_the_United_States), located entirely within [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas), containing the state's five largest cities ([Dallas–Fort Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas–Fort_Worth), [Greater Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Houston), [San Antonio–Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio–Austin)), and home to about two-thirds of the state's population, being connected by [Interstate 45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_45), [Interstate 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_10), and [Interstate 35](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_35).

Thales's theorem states that if , , and are distinct points on a [circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle) where the line is a [diameter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diameter), the [angle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angle) is a [right angle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_angle).
Thomas was an early medieval [Bishop of the East Angles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop_of_the_East_Angles).

time-varying phasors are used for analyzing narrow-band signals, whose signal bandwidths in the [frequency domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frequency_domain) are considerably smaller than the carrier frequency.
Gerald Raphael 'Tip' O'Neill; (October 24, 1898 – December 6, 1984) was a player in the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League) (NFL).

triangle is a [polygon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygon) with three corners and three sides, one of the basic [shapes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shapes) in [geometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geometry).

definition: triangle group is a [group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_(mathematics)) that can be realized geometrically by sequences of [reflections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reflection_(mathematics)) across the sides of a [triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangle).
triangle of opposition is a diagram representing the different ways in which each of the three propositions of the system is logically related ('opposed') to each of the others.
triangular array of numbers, polynomials, or the like, is a doubly indexed sequence in which each row is only as long as the row's own index.
triangulation is the process of determining the location of a point by forming [triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangle)s to the point from known points.

trigonometric functions (also called circular functions, angle functions or goniometric functions) are [real function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_function)s which relate an angle of a [right-angled triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right-angled_triangle) to ratios of two side lengths.
trigonometric interpolation is [interpolation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpolation) with [trigonometric polynomial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trigonometric_polynomial)s.

trigonometric polynomial is a finite [linear combination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_combination) of [functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics)) sin(nx) and cos(nx) with n taking on the values of one or more [natural number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_number)s.

trigonometric tables were essential for [navigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navigation), [science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science) and [engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering).
trigonometry of a tetrahedron are obtained by permutation of the edge lengths.
trilliant cut, sometimes called a trillion, trillian, or Trielle is a [triangular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangle) type of [[Gemstone#Cutting and polishing|gemstone]] cut.
true anomaly is an angular [parameter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parameter) that defines the position of a body moving along a [Keplerian orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keplerian_orbit).
unit circle is a [circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle) of unit [radius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radius)—that is, a radius of [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1).

Wythoff array is an infinite [matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrix_(mathematics)) of [positive integer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positive_integer)s derived from the [Fibonacci sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence) and named after Dutch mathematician [Willem Abraham Wythoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willem_Abraham_Wythoff).
